Flash Loan Attack refers to a loan that is borrowed without collateral and must be repaid within a single blockchain transaction. Flash Loan Attack is used to manipulate prices or governance votes in DeFi protocols. Flash Loan Attack typically exploits temporary imbalances in liquidity pools or price oracles. Flash Loan Attack is executed atomically, so the attacker either completes the full sequence or the transaction reverts.

Liquidation Cascade describes a sequence in which falling collateral prices trigger forced liquidations of borrowing positions. Liquidation Cascade can push asset prices down further, which triggers additional liquidations. Liquidation Cascade can increase losses for borrowers and stress lending protocols.

Sandwich Attack places attacker transactions before and after a victim's trade in the same block. Sandwich Attack profits from the price movement caused by the victim's trade. Sandwich Attack increases the slippage that the victim experiences.

Oracle Attack manipulates the price data supplied to a DeFi protocol by an oracle. Oracle Attack causes the protocol to value collateral or assets incorrectly. Oracle Attack can enable unfair liquidations or undercollateralized borrowing.

51% Attack requires an attacker to control a majority of a blockchain's mining hash power or staking weight. 51% Attack allows the attacker to reverse or block recent transactions. 51% Attack enables double-spending of coins on the affected blockchain.
